title: In Korea, Changing Your Name Is Easy

slides.headline: In Korea, changing your name **is easy.**
slides.note: A court form, a small fee, a few months.

slides.headline: It's called **gaemyeong**
slides.body: 개명, a name change. You file at the court near your home. No lawyer needed, and most people never see a judge.

slides.headline: Once, **almost impossible**
slides.body: Courts used to say no unless a name was truly shameful. In 2005 the Supreme Court ruled that a name belongs to the person who carries it.

slides.headline: Names from **a harder time**
slides.body: Some grandmothers were named Malja (말자), roughly "the last girl", by parents hoping for a son next. Many later changed it.

slides.headline: Teased? **Change it.**
slides.body: A name that sounds like a joke, one shared by half your class, one nobody can spell. Parents apply for their kids too.

slides.headline: Or change it **for luck**
slides.body: Many visit a jakmyeongso (작명소), a naming shop. It picks a new name from your birth date and saju, Korean fortune-telling.

slides.headline: Courts still **say no**
slides.body: If a new name looks like a way to hide a crime or dodge a debt, the request is turned down.

slides.headline: The court fee **to change your name**
slides.body: About 70 cents, plus a few thousand won for mail. You can even file online.

slides.headline: Elsewhere a name is for life. **Here, a fresh start.**
slides.body: In many countries a new name comes with marriage. Korean women keep theirs. Here, people change a name to change their luck.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.

caption:
In Korea, changing your name takes a court form, a small fee and a few months.

Some do it to escape teasing. Many do it for luck.

How hard is it to change your name where you live?
reply: One more: once the court says yes, you have one month to report it at the local office. Then comes the hard part: the bank, the phone, the cards, every account. Would you change your name if it were this easy?
fact_check: 2장: 개명허가 신청은 주소지 관할 가정법원/지방법원. 서면 심리가 대부분. 변호사 불필요.
3장: 대법원 2005.11.16. 2005스26 결정 — 개명은 원칙적으로 허가, 범죄 은폐·법령상 제한 회피 등 불순한 의도면 불허.
4장: '말자'(끝 말+아들 바라는 뜻), '끝순' 등 남아선호 이름. 'roughly'로 의역 표시.
5장: 놀림·흔한 이름·어려운 한자 등 개명 사유. 미성년자는 부모가 법정대리인으로 신청.
6장: 작명소, 사주 기반 작명. 'Many'로 표기, 비율 단정 안 함.
7장: 2005스26 결정의 불허 사유(범죄 은폐, 채무 회피 등).
9장: 한국 여성은 결혼 후 성을 바꾸지 않음(민법상 부부 별성). 타국 일반화는 'many countries'.
1장: 인지대 1,000원+송달료 수준, 처리 보통 1~3개월 → 'a small fee, a few months'.
댓글: 가족관계등록법 — 개명허가 후 1개월 이내 시·구·읍·면에 개명신고.
8장: 민사소송 등 인지법 — 비송사건 신청 인지액 1,000원(개명허가 신청 안내 다수 동일), 송달료 별도 수천 원. 대한민국 법원 전자소송으로 온라인 신청 가능. 1,000원 ≈ US$0.70.
